title: Normalized right-derived comparison for a K-injective-preserving exact square
statement:
Let $\mathcal A',\mathcal A,\mathcal B',\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every complex of $\mathcal A'$ and $\mathcal A$ admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex, meaning a complex $J$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(E,J)=0$ for every acyclic complex $E$; $K$ denotes complexes modulo chain homotopy. Let $H':\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$ and $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive functors. Let $r:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ and $s:\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$ be exact additive functors, with $sH'=Hr$ on objects and morphisms, and assume $r$ carries K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes. Use termwise application on complexes, the canonical exact-functor localization identifications [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and fixed universal total right derived pairs $(RH',\eta')$, $(RH,\eta)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $A=D(s)RH'$ and $B=RH D(r)$.
There is a unique natural isomorphism $\beta:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ such that, for every K-injective complex $J$ of $\mathcal A'$,
$$\beta_{QJ}\circ D(s)(\eta'_J)=\eta_{rJ}.$$
More precisely, $a(J)=D(s)(\eta'_J)$ and $b(J)=\eta_{rJ}$ are isomorphisms with the same source $Q(HrJ)$, the family $\delta(J)=b(J)a(J)^{-1}$ is natural for homotopy classes between K-injective complexes, and for every $M\in D(\mathcal A')$ and every isomorphism $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$ with $J$ K-injective,
$$\beta_M=B(u)^{-1}\delta(J)A(u).$$
This value is independent of $u,J$; uniqueness requires normalization only on K-injectives, not on all complexes. No adjunction or tower structure is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $\lambda_{t,C}:D(t)(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(tC)$ for the natural localization identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], for $t=r,s$. These exist because $r,s$ are exact additive. For a K-injective $J$ of $\mathcal A'$, both $J$ and $rJ$ are K-injective by hypothesis. Thus [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] makes $\eta'_J$ and $\eta_{rJ}$ invertible. With $V(J)=Q(HrJ)=Q(sH'J)$, the fully typed maps are
$$a_J=D(s)(\eta'_J)\circ\lambda_{s,H'J}^{-1}:V(J)\to A(QJ),\qquad b_J=RH(\lambda_{r,J}^{-1})\circ\eta_{rJ}:V(J)\to B(QJ).$$
Functors preserve inverse pairs, so both maps are isomorphisms. Set $\delta_J=b_Ja_J^{-1}$. These are exactly the maps in the statement after its canonical localization identifications.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); explicit exact-square comparison and descent argument

proof.text:
For a homotopy class $h:J\to J'$ between K-injective complexes, write $V(h)=Q(Hr(h))=Q(sH'(h))$. Additivity makes degreewise functors preserve chain homotopies: applying the functor to $h-h'=dk+kd$ gives $F(h)-F(h')=F(d)F(k)+F(k)F(d)$. Thus all these expressions are defined on homotopy classes. Naturality of the units in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and of $\lambda$ in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives
$$A(Qh)a_J=a_{J'}V(h),\qquad B(Qh)b_J=b_{J'}V(h).$$
Multiplying the first equality by $a_{J'}^{-1}$ on the left and $a_J^{-1}$ on the right, and substituting in the second, gives $B(Qh)\delta_J=\delta_{J'}A(Qh)$.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); explicit exact-square comparison and descent argument

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every derived morphism $t:QJ\to QJ'$ between K-injectives is $Qh$ for a unique homotopy class $h:J\to J'$. Step 2 therefore gives
$$B(t)\delta_J=\delta_{J'}A(t)$$
for every such $t$, not merely for images of selected resolution maps. Also every $M\in D(\mathcal A')$ has an isomorphism $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$ with $J$ K-injective: represent $M$ by a complex $C$ in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], choose the assumed quasi-isomorphism $C\to J$, and compose the representing isomorphism $M\cong QC$ with its invertible image under $Q$. This uses arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms, not monomorphic resolutions.

proof.text:
For such $(J,u)$ define $c(M;J,u)=B(u)^{-1}\delta_JA(u)$. To check independence, let $v:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ'$ be another choice and put $t=vu^{-1}:QJ\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ'$. Step 3 gives $B(t)^{-1}\delta_{J'}A(t)=\delta_J$, whence
$$B(v)^{-1}\delta_{J'}A(v)=B(u)^{-1}B(t)^{-1}\delta_{J'}A(t)A(u)=B(u)^{-1}\delta_JA(u).$$
Here $v=tu$ and only functoriality and inverse cancellation are used. Define $\beta_M$ to be this common value; it is an isomorphism because all three factors are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); explicit exact-square comparison and descent argument

proof.text:
For $f:M\to N$ choose $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$ and $v:N\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ'$, and put $t=vfu^{-1}$. Applying step 3 and then functoriality gives
$$B(f)\beta_M=B(v)^{-1}B(t)\delta_JA(u)=B(v)^{-1}\delta_{J'}A(t)A(u)=\beta_NA(f).$$
Thus $\beta:A\Rightarrow B$ is natural. Its inverse components are natural too, by multiplying this equality on the left by $\beta_N^{-1}$ and on the right by $\beta_M^{-1}$; hence it is a natural isomorphism. At $M=QJ$ use the choice $u=1_{QJ}$ to get $\beta_{QJ}=\delta_J$, so $\beta_{QJ}a_J=b_J$, the required normalization. Step 4 supplies the displayed formula of the statement for every $(u,J)$.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); explicit exact-square comparison and descent argument

proof.text:
Let $\gamma:A\Rightarrow B$ be any natural isomorphism satisfying the stated normalization only on K-injectives. Invertibility of $a_J$ gives $\gamma_{QJ}=b_Ja_J^{-1}=\delta_J$. For any $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$, naturality of $\gamma$ gives
$$\gamma_M=B(u)^{-1}\gamma_{QJ}A(u)=B(u)^{-1}\delta_JA(u)=\beta_M.$$
Thus all components agree, proving uniqueness without a normalization assumption on other complexes.
